topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and sets out its learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer evolution and the origins of cancer susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations can produce evolving cancer clones and why their emergence depends on cellular and environmental context.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and the evidence for their influence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental exposures contribute to cancer risk and how that contribution is recognised and interpreted.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive cancer, with Burkitt lymphoma illustrating the interaction between infection and oncogenic change.

topics.label: Environmental carcinogens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental carcinogens produce DNA damage through their activity within the body.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish why mutational initiation may require a subsequent growth-promoting environment for tumours to develop.

topics.label: Developmental and tissue susceptibility, with a synthesis of carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: The explanation of context-dependent susceptibility concludes with a recap of the carcinogenic mechanisms developed in the preceding discussion.

topics.label: Methods for identifying and assessing carcinogenic exposures
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine methods for establishing whether an exposure contributes to cancer and the limitations of the evidence those methods provide.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising its conclusions and placing cancer risks within everyday risk–benefit decisions.
